evidence.description: The authentication-change handler performs login/logout side effects but never updates the published authentication status or profile.
After initialization, authentication status and profile are refreshed only through the separate user-profile update handler.
Seed refresh behavior depends on the potentially stale published isLoggedIn value.

candidates.explanation: A login or logout notification does not synchronize isLoggedIn, userProfile, username, or avatarURL. Unless a separate profile-update notification also arrives, the provider retains the previous authentication display state. In particular, logout resets seed state while potentially leaving isLoggedIn true, causing later refreshes to select the authenticated path.
candidates.title: Authentication notifications leave published authentication state stale

evidence.description: Visit registration launches an untracked task and applies its response after an asynchronous request without checking whether the authentication session has changed.
A completed response directly updates level and progress and can update the seed balance.
Logout resets local state but does not invalidate outstanding visit requests.

candidates.explanation: A visit request started while logged in can complete after logout has reset the provider. Its response is applied unconditionally, restoring the previous session's server balance and level to the logged-out state. Repeated refreshes can also leave multiple requests in flight whose results are applied in completion order rather than request order.
candidates.title: Outstanding visit requests can overwrite state after logout

evidence.description: Each animation schedules unconditional delayed writes to seedCount and balanceIncrement, with no cancellation or check that the update is still current.
Resetting seed state does not invalidate previously scheduled animation callbacks.

candidates.explanation: The balance is not committed until a delayed callback runs. If another update or logout reset occurs during that delay, the older callback can overwrite the newer seed count. Overlapping animations also schedule independent clearing callbacks, so an earlier animation can clear balanceIncrement while a later animation is still active.
candidates.title: Delayed animation callbacks can overwrite newer balance state

evidence.description: The documented logged-out result is an empty string, but the implementation always formats a level number and name without checking authentication status.

candidates.explanation: levelDisplayText always returns a formatted level label, including for logged-out users. This contradicts its explicit documented contract that logged-out users receive an empty string, exposing level text when the property says it should be absent.
candidates.title: Logged-out level text contradicts its declared behavior
